Question
========
Why is it generally recommended to export figures as vector graphics (e.g., PDF or SVG) rather than a raster format
(e.g., PNG or JPEG) for a report?

Answerlist
----------
* Vector formats always produce smaller file sizes than raster formats.
* Vector graphics render crisply at any zoom level or print size, while raster images can look blurry or pixelated when scaled up.
* Vector formats are the only ones supported by Quarto.
* Vector graphics load faster in a web browser than raster images.

Solution
========

Answerlist
----------
* Wrong: file size depends on the image's complexity, not simply on whether it's vector or raster.
* Correct: vector graphics scale without loss of quality, so they stay sharp when zoomed in or printed at a larger size, unlike raster images.
* Wrong: Quarto supports both vector and raster image formats.
* Wrong: load time depends on file size and complexity, not simply on vector versus raster format.
